name: Andreas Vesalius
summary: Flemish anatomist and physician who founded modern human anatomy through direct dissection and publication of De Humani Corporis Fabrica.

name: Andreas Vesalius
summary: Apothecary to Emperor Charles V and father of the anatomist Andreas Vesalius.

name: Isabel Crabbe
summary: Mother of Andreas Vesalius.

name: Girolamo Cardano
summary: Physician and mathematician who cast Vesalius's horoscope.

name: Jacobus Sylvius
summary: Anatomist and teacher of Vesalius at the University of Paris.

name: Guinter of Andernach
summary: Professor of anatomy in Paris and former teacher of Vesalius.

name: Gemma Frisius
summary: Mathematician and friend of Vesalius at Louvain.

name: Johannes Stephanus
summary: Artist from Calcar who drew figures for Vesalius's charts.

name: Joannes Oporinus
summary: Printer in Basel who printed the Fabrica.

name: Charles V
summary: Holy Roman Emperor who employed Vesalius as physician to the imperial household.

name: Philip II
summary: King of Spain whom Vesalius served as physician after Charles V's abdication.

name: Gabriele Fallopio
summary: Anatomist and successor to Vesalius's chair at Padua.

name: Henry II
summary: King of France whose fatal head wound was treated by Vesalius.

name: Don Carlos
summary: Son and heir of Philip II treated by Vesalius for a head injury.

name: University of Louvain
summary: University where Vesalius matriculated in 1530 and received his Bachelor of Medicine.

name: University of Paris
summary: University where Vesalius studied medicine from 1533 to 1536.

name: University of Padua
summary: University where Vesalius received his Doctor of Medicine and held the chair of surgery.

name: University of Bologna
summary: University where Vesalius gave anatomical demonstrations in 1540.

name: Imperial Household
summary: Medical staff of Emperor Charles V.

name: Spanish Court
summary: Court of Philip II where Vesalius served as physician.

name: Brussels
summary: City where Vesalius received elementary education and returned to in 1536.

name: Padua
summary: City where Vesalius studied, taught, and composed the Fabrica.

name: Basel
summary: City where the Fabrica was printed by Oporinus.

name: Spain
summary: Country where Vesalius served Philip II from 1559.

name: Zante
summary: Island where Vesalius died in October 1564.

name: De Humani Corporis Fabrica
summary: Vesalius's seminal anatomical treatise published in 1543.

name: Epitome
summary: A partial digest of the Fabrica intended for beginners.
